name: Haryanvi

ancestors.notes: Descent from Old Indo-Aryan (Sanskrit) via Sauraseni Prakrit and Apabhraṃśa, Western Hindi zone.

Close Western Hindi relative; shares Standard Hindi's Devanagari letter-to-sound conventions (schwa inherent vowel, retroflex/dental contrast). Haryanvi speakers are largely literate in Standard Hindi and often use the Hindi orthographic register for writing.

notes: Haryanvi (Bangaru), spoken mainly in Haryana, India. Western Hindi (Central Indo-Aryan) group. Written in Devanagari, generally following Standard Hindi orthographic conventions (no independent standardised spelling norm), hence graphemes_base=hi. Wikipedia's consonant table shows the same voiceless/voiced/aspirated/breathy-voiced four-way contrast as Hindi. No cited academic source was found describing an orthography distinct from Hindi's, so no overrides are asserted; distinctive Haryanvi phonological facts (e.g. its lexical tone/pitch-accent reported in some dialect descriptions) are not encoded here for lack of a citable grapheme-level source.
